sections.title: Prerequisite: From Discrete to Continuous
lecture_lines: Discrete events use histograms with bars.
Continuous data makes bar width zero.
animations: Create a discrete bar chart showing counts in #FFFFFF using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/histogram.svg].
Transform discrete bars into a smooth curve in #FFD700.
Highlight the area under the resulting curve in #00FFFF using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/histogram.svg].

sections.title: Defining the PDF Curve
lecture_lines: The PDF is a density function.
Total area under curve is one.
animations: Plot a bell-shaped PDF curve in #FFD700.
Highlight the curve area with #FFD700, ensure all values > 0.

sections.title: Calculating Probability as Area
lecture_lines: Probability is area under the curve.
animations: Shade the area under the curve in #00FFFF.
Show a slider moving from x1 to x2 on the axis.
Display integral formula below the curve in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Real-world Application: The Reliable Robot
lecture_lines: The peak shows most likely outcomes.
Area proves reachability of the target.
animations: Show a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] operating within a timeline in #FFFFFF.
Map operation time probability using the PDF curve.
Flash the low-probability failure region in #FF4500 with the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg].

sections.title: Conclusion & Key Takeaways
lecture_lines: PDFs describe probability density, not probability.
Spread outcomes result in flat curves.
animations: Display text: "PDF describes probability density" in #FFFFFF.
Animate a tall peak vs flat curve for comparison.
Show final summary bullet points in #32CD32.
